# block-components

<!-- GENERATED by ./gradlew specReport --write - do not edit. -->

Specification: [SC-150](../../spec/normative/) &middot; 
Ledger: [`spec/coverage/block-components.yaml`](../../spec/coverage/block-components.yaml)

| Feature | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `minecraft:collision_box` | partial | Light occlusion still treats the block as a full cube: a block with a smaller collision box shadows as if it filled its space. That matches how the block is currently DRAWN — every bound block is a unit cube until minecraft:geometry lands — and moving occlusion first would give a block that is visibly a cube and shadows like a slab, which is harder to recognise than the present state. Revisit with geometry, not before. The 1.875-block cap and the requirement that the origin start inside the block are applied by truncation, and neither has been observed on a real Bedrock client; what Bedrock does with a larger box (truncate it, or refuse the block) is unverified. Truncating keeps the block, which is the outcome constitution rule 5 asks for. |
| `minecraft:selection_box` | partial | As minecraft:collision_box, which this shares its reading with. The two are resolved independently — Minecraft falls the collision shape back to the outline shape by default, and sharing one answer would make `"selection_box": false` delete a block's collision as well. |
| `minecraft:geometry` | partial | Path A only (SC-150 section 5.1): a model becomes a Java block model when every bone rotation is a quarter turn about one axis (inherited turns compose along the parent chain) and every cube rotation is one Java can express, which is one axis at -45, -22.5, 22.5 or 45 degrees. Anything else — a free bone rotation, a two-axis turn, a poly mesh, Molang bone_visibility or binding — draws as a plain cube with the block's texture and reports SCE-2031. The block is placeable, breakable and visible in every case; it is the SHAPE that degrades, never the block. A geometry no enabled pack declares is the same fallback with SCE-2030. The Z axis is mirrored on the way to Java and this IS observed — the same block was placed in both editions side by side. Everything is computed in Bedrock's space and converted once, so north and south trade places and no face is flipped or spun. The DIRECTION of a quarter turn is observed too, and it was wrong until it was: a Bedrock angle turns the opposite way round to a right-handed turn about the same axis. A block orienting one geometry through four permutations at 0, 90, 180 and -90 degrees came out with its east and west placements holding each other's rotation while north and south were right, which is the only symptom a wrong sense can have — a half turn is the same either way. Faces carry no cullface, so a face that could have been hidden by a neighbour is drawn. That costs a quad and cannot produce a hole; the reverse can. |
| `minecraft:unit_cube` | partial | A block with no geometry, one naming minecraft:geometry.full_block, and one whose geometry cannot be transpiled all draw the same unit cube. The first two are exact; the third is SC-150 section 5.2's fallback and is a wrong shape rather than a wrong block. |
| `minecraft:transformation` | stub | Rotation, scale and translation applied to the model. Applied at bake for Path A. |
| `minecraft:material_instances` | partial | Only the texture is read. Every block draws on the same render layer whatever its render_method says, so a block declaring alpha_test or blend is opaque: a texture with transparent pixels shows black where it should show through, and one with partial alpha shows none of it. That is the next thing to fix in this entry and it is independent of geometry. A face naming an instance the block does not declare falls back to `*` rather than losing its texture, which is one typo costing nothing. |
